Hi Samir — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise benchmark sprint plan we propose; happy to iterate. Attachment: benchmark-plan-v1.pdf (summary + test matrix).

Acceptance gateway (high level):
- Functional checks (smoke): correct model responses on canonical prompts, error rates < 0.5%
- Latency: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms, p99 < 600ms (measured at application edge after routing)
- Throughput: sustained 200 requests/sec (single-region reserved capacity), burstable up to 400 rps for 5 minutes
- Concurrency: graceful behavior up to 1,000 concurrent sessions; no single-request tail that causes downstream queueing
- Stability: no more than 1 server restart or preempt in a 4-hour test window

Load-test plan (three phases):
1) Warmup & functional (30–60 min): low RPS + KV cache priming using a 3k prompt seed set (we'll provide)
2) Ramp & steady (2–3 hours): linear ramp to 200 RPS, hold for 60 min, collect token-level cost and latency histograms
3) Stress & fallback (1 hour): spike tests to 400 RPS and controlled instance failures to validate fallbacks to smaller model variant

Tools & artifacts:
- We will provide k6 load scripts + expected response validator (open-source) and a sample traffic profile.
- Redwood will share: raw token logs (anonymized), aggregated latency percentiles, GPU utilization charts, and a post-test runbook.

Success criteria & sign-off:
- Pass all functional checks
- p95 latency below 250ms during steady phase
- No unhandled errors above 1%
- Customer verifies outputs on 100 canonical prompts (we'll provide a shared sheet)

Timeline & POC:
- Proposed sprint: Nov 30–Dec 3 (on-site window optional; remote OK)
- Redwood POC: Hannah Schmitt (CS lead) and Dev Patel (runtime lead)
- Customer POC: Samir Patel (eng), Elena Cruz (product)

Next step: confirm the sprint week and whether Orion wants Redwood to run tests from our hosted endpoints or provide k6 scripts for you to run in your environment.

Thanks — attaching the plan.

Best,

--

Quick technical notes / clarifications: Attachment: test-traffic-profile.json (traffic buckets + token distributions)

- Model variants: during stress we will route to the quantized 8-bit variant for throughput; p95 may increase slightly (expect ~20–30ms uplift). We'll capture per-variant percentiles in the run artifacts.
- Cache priming: please confirm whether you want prefix caching enabled for canonical prompts; we recommend enabling for steady-state tests to reflect production-like savings.
- Autoscaling: Dedicated pool will have reserved capacity for the steady phase; we will simulate preemption in the stress phase (one GPU down) to validate graceful reroute to warm spare.
- Observability hooks: we will expose a short-term tracing token so your team can correlate requests (no PII).

If you prefer, Redwood can host the load test and share logs; otherwise we'll hand over k6 scripts and instructions. Either way we'll need a shared Drive link for artifacts.
